title: Masonic funerals and the funeral team
summary: Caldwell describes the well-conducted masonic funerals and eleven funerals in 1959.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: I -- I mean the three or four masonic funerals I've seen uptown have been very well done and very impressively done.
Yeah, they is only about one hour long. Now, it's only about one hour.
Yeah, but I mean they've been very well conducted, with dignity, because, after all, you know, you can -- with the best will in the world (unintelligible) you could goof up in (unintelligible).
I mean you could learn all that stuff, but you're still going to slip up, get nervous (unintelligible), --

Very well. They have a regular what you call team for -- to substitute anytime they do funeral [two times.] Between Kenneth Roane- he's past master (unintelligible) Dial, he's past master, he would do the funeral (table). We would do the other parts with him. And one time we had funerals back to back. Had to and do one on a Monday, me on a Tuesday. We had -- that year, in 1959, we had 11 funerals. And we had to participate in all those funerals. So between Harry Dial and Lem Johnson they'll alternate (unintelligible) doing Roane these funerals, because and I, we were stuck with the warden's part, so we just did the part that's -- every time they had a (unintelligible) the funeral, 11 of them that year. I only had one funeral when I was a master. I was very lucky.
